walkthroughs.body_html:
Human rights are freedoms every person has — just by being human.

The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN in 1948, after WW2.

It has 30 articles: right to life, freedom from torture, freedom of belief, fair trial, and more.

Christianity teaches all humans are made in the image of God (Genesis 1:27) — so all have equal dignity.

Islam: Allah created all people equal, regardless of race or wealth (Qur'an 49:13).

Both religions push back when human rights are denied — defending the poor, refugees, and the oppressed.

Religious freedom = the right to hold and practise any belief — or none.

The Qur'an: 'There is no compulsion in religion' (2:256).

Christianity protected by Article 18 of the UDHR. In some countries today, Christians, Muslims, Jews and others face persecution. Religious leaders campaign for freedom of conscience everywhere.

mcqs.q: 'There is no compulsion in religion' is from:
options: The Bible
The Qur'an
The Torah
The UN Charter

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: The Buddha created the universe.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Jesus was half God and half human.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
The Buddha created the universe.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.
